messages.subject: bounds on random effects.
messages.body_plain:
Hi there,

I am wondering if there Is a command that would allow me to put bounds on random effects for the the inner optimization?

If not, would it be common to penalize/discourage the model sampling in an unlikely space? for example in a fisheries model I want to stop the model from attempting candidate values of high F (fishing mortality). What would be the best TMB configuration for such a scenario?

Regards,
Craig

messages.subject: Re: bounds on random effects.
messages.body_plain:
Hi Craig,

in situations where I have needed to bound parameters to an
interval (a,b) I have used a scaled and translated log-odds
transform. i.e., to bound u to (a,b) I would model it as,

PARAMETER(stlogit_u);

then back-transform to get u

Type u = a + (b - a)*invlogit(stlogit_u);

messages.subject: Normalized residuals for use in ACF plotting
messages.subject_clean: Normalized residuals for use in ACF plotting
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

I hope I've found the appropriate place for this query.

I've been using glmmTMB to implement beta GLMMs. I'm working with datasets that comprise measures made from the same plots at regular three month intervals.

I would like to use ACF plots to look at possible temporal auto-correlation in the residuals, and in the event that I need to include a correlation structure (e.g. AR1), I would like to see how well it accounts for the auto-correlation.

I read here <https://stats.stackexchange.com/questions/80823/do-autocorrelated-residual-patterns-remain-even-in-models-with-appropriate-corre> and here <http://bbolker.github.io/mixedmodels-misc/ecostats_chap.html#gopher-tortoise>, that it is necessary to use the normalized residuals for ACF plotting, rather than the raw residuals, as the raw residuals contain no information on any correlation terms.
The information in the residuals.glm help file also implies that pearson/standardized residuals may be no good for this(?):

type: an optional character string specifying the type of residuals
      to be used. If ‘"response"’, the "raw" residuals (observed -
      fitted) are used; else, if ‘"pearson"’, the standardized
      residuals (raw residuals divided by the corresponding
      standard errors) are used; else, if ‘"normalized"’, the
      normalized residuals (standardized residuals pre-multiplied
      by the inverse square-root factor of the estimated error
      correlation matrix) are used. Partial matching of arguments
      is used, so only the first character needs to be provided.
      Defaults to ‘"response"’.

The question: Since the residuals.glmmTMB function currently only accepts "response" or "pearson" as 'type' arguments, does anyone know of a way to derive the normalized residuals by hand?

Apologies if I have misunderstood any concepts here, I am new to analysing time series data.

Many thanks,
Helen
